tasks.short: Set merchandise pricing policies that meet margin goals and fit local trading conditions.

steps.what: Collect merchandise costs, sales, stock and current prices.
Calculate margins and compare possible price ladders.
Choose margin floors, markdown triggers and local exceptions with the store manager.
Write the policy, worked examples and exception instructions.
Approve the policy within delegated commercial authority.
Enter approved pricing rules and effective dates.

tasks.design: A scheduled integration joins costs, sales, stock and price history from the {ERP} and {OPS_SYSTEM}; a deterministic calculator feeds pricing scenarios to the {BI}. Structured policy choices generate a document in the {DOCS}, and configured approvals release validated pricing rules to the {OPS_SYSTEM}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Cost, stock and price histories use different identifiers. Local policy choices often exist only in documents.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing pricing controls, structured templates and faster integration development make the calculator and release checks affordable. No model breakthrough is needed.
tasks.still_hard: Cost allocation, supplier funding, uncertain demand response and inconsistent price history can distort apparent margins.
tasks.human_edge: Judge customer expectations, competitive positioning and when protecting a relationship outweighs a short-term margin gain.

ambition.what: Weekly markdown-window decisions for slow-moving merchandise

tasks.altitude: The supervisor spends less time reconciling figures and writing policy. They can propose weekly markdown changes within approved limits; wider pricing authority needs explicit delegation.

reach.task: Compare category pricing scenarios against store contribution targets.
reach.learn: Contribution margins, demand uncertainty and the limits of price-response estimates.

evidence.claim: Joining retail records, calculating margins and generating policy templates are deterministic implementation patterns.
Applicable EU price-reduction announcements generally require the lowest prior 30-day price; exceptions and national implementation need checking.

assumptions: The supervisor proposes local policy within centrally defined commercial limits.
The time split represents a policy review cycle; daily work usually concerns exceptions.
Existing pricing configuration can express floors, effective dates and approval limits.
Build ranges cover one store format and a small set of connected systems.
unknowns: Who may approve pricing policies and customer-facing price changes?
Are costs, taxes, supplier rebates and price histories reliable at merchandise level?
Which local changes are allowed under central pricing policy?
Can current systems stage and reverse approved pricing changes?
research_questions: Which price-announcement exceptions and national rules apply to the merchandise categories?
Can existing pricing configuration cover every required rule before custom code is built?
new_work: Investigate missing costs and unmatched merchandise identifiers.
Review scenario assumptions and unintended margin effects.
Maintain policy templates, approval limits and prior-price checks.
Monitor released prices and reverse faulty changes.

tasks.short: Hire, develop and evaluate retail staff, with human decisions on promotion and dismissal.

steps.what: Define the vacancy and required skills from staffing needs.
Interview shortlisted candidates and record job-related evidence.
Select a candidate and approve proposed employment terms.
Prepare and send the approved employment offer.
Create the employee record after offer acceptance.
Assign required courses and plan supervised shop-floor practice.
Demonstrate selling skills, observe practice and give feedback.
Gather sales results, training completion and documented observations for evaluation.
Discuss performance, hear the employee's account and agree development actions.
Decide whether to recommend promotion, formal support or dismissal.
Check evidence and national procedures, then approve or return the proposed action.
Explain the approved action privately to the employee.

tasks.design: Configure vacancy templates, approved offer generation and starter workflows across the {ATS}, {ESIGN} and {HCM}, with role-based course assignment in the {LMS}. A deterministic evidence pack joins authorised records from the {OPS_SYSTEM}, {LMS} and {TALENT}; managers conduct interviews, coaching and employment decisions, while the {WORKFLOW} routes approvals and follow-up records.
tasks.previous_blocker: Recruitment, learning and performance records sit in separate systems. Managers bridge them manually, while employment decisions require contextual evidence.
tasks.enabler_now: Configured workflows and inexpensive connectors can reuse approved records and templates. Automated scoring or a model is unnecessary for this scope.
tasks.still_hard: Sales attribution, unequal shift opportunities, incomplete observations and national employment procedures complicate fair evaluation.
tasks.human_edge: Build trust, recognise improvement, hear explanations and take responsibility for consequential employment decisions.

ambition.what: A structured first-month coaching programme for new retail staff

tasks.altitude: Less paperwork creates time for observed practice and earlier support conversations. Hiring, promotion and dismissal authority remains with the existing authorised roles.

reach.learn: Fair comparisons, opportunity differences and evidence-based coaching.

reach.task: Mentor a new starter during supervised selling practice.
reach.learn: Demonstration, specific feedback and checking understanding.

evidence.claim: Approved templates, course assignment and factual evidence assembly can use configured workflows and deterministic integrations.
Experiments with fintech sales agents found manager-relayed AI feedback performed better than either alone; this is not retail-specific evidence.
The Netherlands has works-council consent provisions covering specified employee-data and performance-observation schemes.
The AI Act identifies specified employment evaluation and task-allocation uses as high-risk; introducing those uses requires a separate assessment.
GDPR Article 22 restricts solely automated decisions with legal or similarly significant effects, subject to its conditions and exceptions.

assumptions: This is a branched personnel lifecycle; hiring, routine reviews and dismissal do not happen in every instance.
Time shares represent the task across a typical mix of cases, including supporting roles.
The design assembles existing evidence without automated candidate ranking, employee scoring or inferred traits.
Consultation and access ranges include possible employee representation review under national rules.
Existing approved templates and retention rules are available.
unknowns: Which hiring and personnel decisions are delegated to the supervisor?
Which national employment rules and collective agreements apply?
What consultation or consent is required for the proposed employee-data use?
Can sales results be attributed fairly to individuals?
Which records may each manager access, and for how long?
Are recruitment shortlisting and personnel record updates handled centrally?
research_questions: What consultation is required under the applicable national rules?
If scope later includes AI evaluation, what classification and obligations apply under current EU law?
Verify the digest's cited AI Act amendment and application dates before relying on its timeline.
new_work: Check evidence packs for attribution errors and missing context.
Maintain role profiles, course mappings and employment templates.
Handle employee corrections and disputed records.
Review access permissions, retention and connector failures.
Coordinate required employee consultation before changing data use.

tasks.short: Coordinate retail promotions, prepare advertising copy and arrange merchandise displays.

steps.what: Review the campaign brief, stock availability and previous promotion results.
Agree the local offer, audience, budget and display concept with marketing.
Write advertising copy and display instructions using approved campaign materials.

loop.input: Approved product facts, offer terms, channel limits, brand guidance and local campaign plan.
loop.output: Channel copy variants and a draft display instruction sheet.
loop.check: Validate prices, dates and required terms against structured inputs; a person checks claims and clarity.
loop.stop: Generate once and allow one revision; missing facts or failed checks return to manual drafting.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates cover standard offers; varied local wording and narrative instructions need bounded drafting.

steps.what: Approve claims, offer terms, brand fit and display materials.
Assign setup duties and confirm materials and deadlines with staff.
Schedule approved digital advertisements and posts.
Arrange merchandise, signage and promotional fixtures on the shop floor.
Inspect the display and authorise opening it to customers.
Review campaign sales, stockouts and advertising results.

tasks.design: A campaign form in the {WORKFLOW} combines approved materials from the {DOCS} with stock and price checks from the {OPS_SYSTEM}; a bounded drafting loop prepares local copy. Approved packs create setup tasks in the {PROJECT} and staged releases in the {ADS} and {SOCIAL}, while the {BI} joins campaign results and store sales.
tasks.previous_blocker: Local copy, central approvals and physical setup follow different paths. Repeated checking ties up the supervisor.
tasks.enabler_now: Reusable campaign packs, configured publishing approvals and bounded text drafting reduce preparation work with existing capabilities.
tasks.still_hard: Physical setup, local judgement, missing materials and separating promotion effects from normal trading remain difficult.
tasks.human_edge: Judge whether a display attracts customers, fits the store and can be delivered by the available team.

ambition.what: A stock-aware local promotion pack for each store

tasks.altitude: The supervisor spends less time adapting copy and chasing materials, leaving more time for the shop floor. Local offer and budget authority remains within existing limits.

reach.task: Run a product demonstration linked to the local promotion.
reach.learn: Audience needs, product claims and practical demonstration planning.
Baseline selection, stockout effects and the limits of campaign attribution.

evidence.claim: Campaign templates, approval routing, scheduled publishing and joined reporting can use existing configuration and deterministic code.
Bounded text generation can prepare copy variants, with factual checks and human approval before publication.
Applicable EU discount announcements require prior-price checks; category exceptions and national implementation need validation.

assumptions: Central marketing provides approved assets and brand guidance.
The supervisor coordinates local execution; specialist staff may operate digital channels.
Setup time includes work performed by retail salespersons.
Standard campaigns use templates without a model; the loop serves variable local copy.
Physical displays are assembled before the supervisor releases them to customers.
unknowns: Which channels and budgets are controlled locally?
Are product facts and approved claims available as reusable records?
Can advertising platforms stage campaigns for approval?
Are stock and price history available at store level?
Are customer segments involved, and what permissions govern their use?
research_questions: Which existing channel tools already support the required approval and scheduling flow?
Which national rules apply to the planned offers and advertising claims?
new_work: Review draft copy for unsupported claims and awkward local wording.
Maintain approved product facts, templates and required terms.
Resolve missing stock, materials and failed publishing jobs.
Check live advertisements against the approved pack.
Review whether reported results reflect actual incremental contribution.

tasks.short: Propose store credit policies and operating procedures within finance and legal limits.

steps.what: Review overdue balances, credit losses and recurring operational exceptions.
Compare current procedures with central policy and documented exceptions.

loop.input: Versioned central policy, local procedures and documented exception descriptions.
loop.output: Proposed gap list with source passages and unresolved questions.
loop.check: Require a source passage for every gap; the supervisor verifies meaning and completeness.
loop.stop: One comparison and one correction pass; conflicting or missing sources go to the policy owner.
loop.why_not_simpler: Document comparison detects changed text, but equivalent or conflicting prose requires interpretation.

steps.what: Agree proposed credit limits, escalation points and operating responsibilities with finance.
Draft procedures, exception routes and staff checklists.

loop.input: Structured policy choices, approved central policy and procedure template.
loop.output: Procedure draft and staff checklist with linked policy sources.
loop.check: Validate limits and roles against structured choices; reviewers check completeness and exception wording.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision; unresolved policy conflicts block approval and return to finance.
loop.why_not_simpler: Template fields cover fixed limits; varied exception procedures need prose adapted to local operations.

steps.what: Approve the policy after required legal review.
Configure approved credit controls and publish the effective procedure.
Brief staff on changed procedures and practise handling exceptions.

tasks.design: A deterministic dashboard joins receivables and operational exceptions from the {ERP} and {OPS_SYSTEM}; bounded document comparison and drafting use approved sources in the {DOCS}. The {WORKFLOW} routes finance and legal review, stages configured controls in the {ERP}, and publishes a versioned procedure only after approval.
tasks.previous_blocker: Policy documents and operational exceptions are disconnected. Translating prose into consistent procedures and controls takes repeated manual work.
tasks.enabler_now: Versioned records, configured credit controls and bounded document processing can support the work without autonomous credit decisions.
tasks.still_hard: Credit authority, consumer versus business credit, conflicting procedures and national rules determine what local policy may change.
tasks.human_edge: Balance commercial access, financial exposure and fair treatment, and recognise when an exception needs specialist advice.

ambition.what: Monthly review of recurring credit-policy exceptions

tasks.altitude: The supervisor brings a clearer exception picture and a prepared procedure draft to finance. They gain time to improve operating practices; credit approval authority does not change automatically.

reach.task: Check account-opening completeness and route credit exceptions.
reach.learn: Required evidence, approval limits and handling sensitive customer records.

reach.task: Resolve orders blocked by approved credit controls.
reach.learn: Payment status, release authority and escalation procedures.

evidence.claim: Receivables summaries, rule validation and approval routing can use deterministic code and existing configuration.
Bounded document comparison and drafting can prepare policy changes, with source checks and specialist approval.
GDPR Article 22 can apply to solely automated credit decisions concerning individuals when its significance conditions are met.

assumptions: The retailer offers account credit; otherwise the credit-policy portion may not apply.
Finance retains final credit-policy authority, while the supervisor proposes local procedures.
Weekly activity is usually exception review; formal policy changes are less frequent.
The scope excludes automated personal creditworthiness assessment and individual credit approval.
Access estimates include finance and legal review; employee consultation applies if employee-data use changes.
unknowns: Does the store offer consumer credit, business account credit or only third-party financing?
Which credit and operating policies may the supervisor change?
Who owns legal review and final approval?
Can current controls represent the approved limits and exception routes?
What customer and employee information appears in exception records?
research_questions: Which EU and national credit rules apply to the actual financing arrangement?
Would any proposed expansion into personal credit assessment trigger additional AI Act obligations?
Can existing configuration replace a custom credit-control application?
new_work: Verify policy comparisons against authoritative source versions.
Resolve ambiguous exceptions with finance and legal specialists.
Maintain structured limits, approval routes and procedure templates.
Test configured controls before release and review false blocks.
Handle staff questions and retire superseded procedures.

role.altitude: The supervisor spends less time collecting records, drafting documents and re-entering approved changes. More of the week goes to shop-floor coaching, commercial choices and resolving exceptions; formal employment, credit and pricing authority changes only through explicit delegation.
reach: Support sales managers with comparable pricing and promotion scenarios.
Help retail salespersons develop structured mentoring skills.
Work with new accounts clerks and order clerks on credit exceptions.
skills_to_grow: Margin analysis and cautious interpretation of promotion results
Structured coaching and fair performance evaluation
Writing clear policy choices and exception routes
Checking source evidence and generated drafts
Understanding approval limits, GDPR and applicable national rules
role.ambitious_version: Become a store improvement lead who combines weekly trading decisions, a first-month coaching programme and regular exception reviews, within delegated commercial and personnel authority.

job.title: First-Line Supervisors of Retail Sales Workers
